title: protocol for structured fragment acknowledgement and tool-call rate limiting acceptance
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define acceptance criteria and rollout plan for a fragment-acknowledgement protocol for streamed structured responses and stricter tool-call rate-limiting semantics. Goal: reduce unrecoverable partial outputs and accidental duplicate tool invocations while preserving low-latency streaming for real-time UX.
background: We have recurring incidents where long streamed structured outputs terminate partially or contain out-of-order fragments when downstream parsers crash or network flaps occur. Separately, aggressive model retries and rapid replays have caused duplicate tool invocations in customer integrations. This ticket specifies an interoperable protocol (handshake, fragment IDs, acks, trailer) and matching acceptance tests plus rate-limiting headers/policies for tool gateways.
acceptance_criteria: Handshake: Client and server negotiate a 'fragmented-structure' capability during initial stream setup using a JSON capability header. If client does not support fragment ack, server falls back to 'best-effort' streaming mode with a warning envelope.

Fragment metadata: Every structured fragment emitted in a stream MUST include a monotonic fragment_id (string) and sequence_index (integer) and MAY include a partial_checksum (hex). Example fragment envelope documented in design doc.

Idempotency token: All tool invocation frames MUST include an idempotency_key (UUID v4). Gateways reject calls without idempotency_key when idempotency_required=true and return error code 412 with explanation.

Acknowledgements: Clients that advertise support MUST send periodic ack frames referencing the highest contiguous sequence_index received. Server will retain replay buffers for unacked fragments up to ack_retention_ms (configurable, default 60s).

Backpressure behavior: If client acks fall behind configured lag_threshold, server will reduce emission rate and emit a 'backpressure' control frame. Emission must resume progressively when ack gap < resume_threshold.

Partial-finalization: Streams that cannot fully assemble into a valid schema due to dropped fragments must emit a final envelope with status: one of [complete, partial_recoverable, partial_irrecoverable, aborted] and an array of missing fragment_ids (empty if complete).

Tool-call error taxonomy: Gateways distinguish: retryable (5xx transient), idempotent-missed (duplicate-prevention failure), hard-fail (4xx bad-args), and throttled. Documentation lists error codes and recommended client strategies.

Rate limiting headers: Tool gateways must honor X-Tool-Rate-Limit, X-Tool-Rate-Remaining, and X-Tool-Reset headers on synchronous responses. SDK surfaces these headers to customers and exposes a backoff helper.

No-duplicate guarantee: For idempotency_key-based calls, system guarantees at-most-once execution within idempotency_window (configurable, default 24h) provided the caller retries using the same idempotency_key. Acceptance test verifies no duplicate side-effects under simulated retries.

Streaming trailer: Every stream MUST finish with a signed trailer envelope containing final_status, emitted_fragment_count, total_schema_root_hash, and optional telemetry pointer. Trailers are validated by client SDK by default.

Observability: Implement telemetry events for fragment_emitted, fragment_ack_received, fragment_replayed, tool_call_invoked, tool_call_deduped, tool_call_rejected. Dashboards must expose ack-lag percentiles and duplicate-invocation rate.
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope serialization/deserialization including fragment_id and checksums.
Integration: end-to-end simulated consumer with flaky network asserting that when acks stop the server emits backpressure and then resumes after recovery.
Chaos: kill parser mid-stream and verify final trailer contains partial_irrecoverable with list of missing fragments and no duplicate tool calls were executed.
Load: run tool gateway under QPS spike with idempotency_on and assert deduplication success rate >= 99.9% and throttle responses follow header contract.
Compatibility: SDK v3.x should gracefully downgrade to 'best-effort' when fragment-ack capability absent and log a single warning per connection.
qa_steps: Follow integration test harness in /confluence/structured-output/tests to run the ack/backpressure scenario.
Use local tool-gateway stub to exercise idempotency token paths and confirm headers appear in responses.
Manual: create a small chat app that requests long JSON array outputs and intentionally drop packets via tc to observe trailer and partial statuses.
Verify dashboards: ack-lag p50/p95, duplicate-invocation rate, and trailer-validation-failures are visible for the test tenants.
monitoring: New metrics: rwd.fragment.ack_lag_ms, rwd.fragment.unacked_count, rwd.tool.duplicate_invocation_count, rwd.tool.idempotency_hit_rate.
Alerts: ack_lag_p95 > 5000ms for 2m => P1 on-call; duplicate_invocation_rate > 0.1% over 15m => investigate gateway misconfiguration.
Logs: fragment envelopes must be traceable by trace_id and fragment_id; include sample query for retrieving the last N fragments for a stream ID.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Enable fragment-ack on 3% of hosted API traffic for 48h with verbose logging and automatic rollback if ack_lag_p95 increases > 2x baseline.
Phase 2 (gradual): Expand to 25% over 7 days while monitoring deduplication metrics and client downgrade rates.
Phase 3 (GA): Flip default to fragment-ack enabled for new streams; keep best-effort available for legacy clients. Announce SDK patch release and migration guide.
tradeoffs: Stronger guarantees (at-most-once) require replay buffers and larger memory retention per stream which increases per-connection cost. We'll default to 60s retention but make it configurable per-account.
Requiring idempotency_key for all tool calls increases client complexity but prevents costly duplicated side-effects; for SDK-first customers we will surface helpers to generate and persist keys.
Trailer signing adds CPU overhead; we'll sign only for streams above a configurable size threshold to balance cost/benefit initially.
decision_log: 2026-02-17: Agreed on UUID v4 idempotency_key and 24h default idempotency_window (Decision by PM + Infra + Security).
2026-02-24: Chose conservative ack_retention_ms=60000 and backpressure resume_threshold=30 fragments after engineering perf tests.
2026-03-05: Opted to implement trailer signing with HMAC-SHA256 and include telemetry pointer rather than full payload. Security reviewed.
notes: SDK teams requested an opt-out flag to preserve existing apps; added to rollout plan.
Security asked for HMAC trailer signing and provided key-rotation guidance; see decision log.
Product to prepare migration comms and example migration code for concurrency models in mobile SDKs.
